gap_analysis: SOL design (per row, r24 one wave of 384 one-CTA rows): bound = one read of the row's 68 KB of bf16 logits (L2-resident after the logits kernel; all bytes in flight at once) + ONE dependent NVLink round + a short local merge; floor ~ load latency + round + ~2 us. Measured v2 chain at r24 (microbench, clock stamps): sample 2.2 + theta 0.7 + candidate pass 10.8 (3-4 serial memory latencies: batches of 4 groups/thread) + message build 3.7 (~12 synced steps, single-thread band search) + round 4.3 + resolve 7.0 + WRITE 4.0 = 34.7 us vs model 9.4. In-step 49 us: the kernel starts right at the logits kernel's end (no hidden PDL overlap), so the extra ~14 us over the microbench is in-kernel (diagnosing with in-step stats/stamps). Redesign: (1) register-resident row: the row's groups are loaded speculatively before its lengths are known (one latency for both), sample/theta/candidates from registers; (2) candidates compacted in POSITION order by a (slot, warp, lane) scan (no bitmap pass later); (3) KV-slot gather of every candidate in the round's shadow; post-round = resolve + one packed scan + scatter; (4) pollers back off (spinning warps steal issue slots and L2 from co-resident rows); (5) message build and resolve collapsed to ~3 synced steps each, no single-thread loops. Projection r24 microbench ~1.5 load + 1 sample/theta/cand + 1.5 message + 3-4 round + 2.5 resolve/write = ~10-11 us (target 11 in-step).
